📢 Special: First-time publication of Father, Love, Son ◀️ KHAMENEI.IR media is publishing, as follows, the letter of the Imam, the Mujahid martyr, His Eminence Grand Ayatollah Khamenei — may his lofty position be elevated — to his son Ayatollah Seyyed Mostafa Khamenei, written during his presence at the fronts of the Sacred Defense.◀️ The text and handwriting of the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution, written on 7 Mordad 1365 and now published on the occasion of #Sacred_Defense_Week, are as follows. entry.title: [FarsNA] What are the consequences of fabricated polarizations for Iran?🔹Reducing the…
entry.summary:

Source: @FarsNA

What are the consequences of fabricated polarizations for Iran?🔹Reducing the country's complex issues to binaries like "peace-seeking vs. warmongering" or "negotiation vs. war" can steer society away from a genuine conversation about national interests, costs, and foreign policy options.🔹Critics of this approach argue that negotiation should be a tool of foreign policy, not the only solution; just as defense and deterrence capabilities should not be equated with "warmongering."🔹The experience of the JCPOA and America's withdrawal from it has brought into sharper focus the debate over guaranteeing an agreement's implementation, reciprocal concessions, and preserving bargaining power. From this perspective, the core issue is not "negotiation or war," but preserving the power of choice and securing national interests.🔹False polarizations, rather than strengthening national cohesion, can deepen social divides; whereas in the face of external threats, internal cohesion, defense capability, economic strength, and active diplomacy can all serve national interests simultaneously.🔹Analysts believe that negotiation can help secure national interests when it is pursued from a position of choice, not out of compulsion and necessity. The experience of past agreements has also shown that an agreement alone, without guarantees of implementation and bargaining power, does not necessarily lead to a sustainable outcome.🔹When individuals and factions are categorized with labels like "warmonger" or "peacenik," the possibility of rational dialogue about details diminishes.🔹From the perspective of critics of polarization, a society that can discuss its differences while emphasizing shared national interests will have a greater capacity to manage foreign crises.@Farspolitics - link

IRGC: We seized the second American unmanned submarine in the Strait of Hormuz

The Naval Force of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed in a statement on Sunday, the fifth of Mehr, that it had identified and seized an American unmanned remotely operated underwater vehicle (UUV) in the Strait of Hormuz.

The IRGC statement said that its Naval Force personnel, in a "coordinated and complex operation" employing intelligence superiority and electronic warfare, trapped the subsurface vehicle, which was operating "to spy in the Strait of Hormuz."

The IRGC identified the submarine as a REMUS 600 and said it has taken it as a prize and it is now in the hands of IRGC Naval Force specialists so its data can be extracted and examined.

Media affiliated with the Islamic Republic also simultaneously released a video of the subsurface vehicle, presenting it as the "second" American UUV, or unmanned submarine, to have fallen into Iran's hands during the recent clashes in the Strait of Hormuz.

According to Iranian state media reports, this submarine is an autonomous underwater vehicle (UUV/AUV), and unlike a manned submarine, it carries no crew on board. This family of systems is used for missions including reconnaissance and countering naval mines, mapping the seabed, subsurface identification and surveillance, and gathering maritime intelligence.

Today's IRGC claim comes after, on the 17th of Shahrivar, the IRGC Naval Force had previously announced the seizure of another American subsurface vehicle near the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz.

CENTCOM said at the time that the submarine had stopped due to a technical malfunction and "did not contain sensitive information."

After several rounds of failed military operations and the humiliation that followed, the enemy's guard shifted to economic siege and hostility. But unfortunately, some managers, advisers, and analysts still deal with it through the negotiation guard (the catalyst of the enemy's plot).

Certainly, military threats must not be neglected or underestimated. But neither should the enemy's intensified helplessness be forgotten, nor should it be given excessive weight, breeding passivity and fear, and causing neglect of a decisive response to the economic war and siege.

When the war happened, the illusion that negotiation and agreement serve as a deterrent defense shield collapsed. Therefore, one must not again create a bubble for oneself and others and retreat into a shell of passivity; for this behavior amounts to being played by the worn-out tactic of the madman.

The economic siege (maritime and aerial), backed by military action, is a one hundred percent aggressive and criminal military action that must be answered by deploying all kinds of military and non-military threats, symmetrical and asymmetrical.

The enemy has targeted your economy; you too must forcefully strike at its economic interests and Achilles' heels in the commercial and energy domains, the infrastructure related to undersea cables, and... in the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandab, the Indian Ocean, the Sea of Oman, and the Persian Gulf.

When your…
entry.summary:

Deterrent Defense Shield: Negotiation or Counter-Offensive? – 1

When your opponent in a contest—a fight—changes stance, you too must change your stance and not remain passive.

America and Israel had clearly come up short in the forty-day war, and the tide had turned, prompting them to seek a ceasefire through intermediaries:

- National unity and cohesion, contrary to the plan for the January overthrow and coup, had been revived and reached its peak.
- The Strait of Hormuz had been closed, humiliating America.
- A significant portion of their offensive and defensive munitions had run out or been strategically depleted.
- Key American bases in the region had been struck. They had nearly been rendered inoperable, yet were still imposing considerable costs on the Pentagon.
- Dozens of fighter jets, helicopters, and drones had been shot down.
- Attempts to reopen the strait or penetrate deep into Iran had failed.
- Iran kept revealing new intelligence and military cards.
- Oil prices during the war had risen to $126.
- And more...

One can accept that, for certain considerations, the Iranian side agreed to a (temporary) ceasefire and would use this time to regroup and reorganize forces, capabilities, and plans.

What is not reasonable was tying the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to the ceasefire.

There was no reason that, while the hostile party had twice betrayed during negotiations and committed great and unprecedented crimes, it should receive a concession on the level of reopening the strait through that strange tweet by Mr. Araghchi.

What was America's reaction? Trump, at the same time as oil prices crashed, announced he would impose a naval blockade against Iran!

This, even though at the height of the war, under pressure from oil prices, he had been forced to suspend some oil sanctions so that Iranian oil could reach the market.

If the justification is an existential threat, Trump later raised this threat more than ten more times. And before that, he never shied away from any crime—unless he was unable to commit it.

Delving into the rest of the story regarding the "memorandum of understanding" is beyond the scope of this analysis.

Whatever judgment we hold about the memorandum of understanding—whether we call it an "honor—a great achievement" or deem it a "mirage/deception operation"—unfortunately, the stance of some of those in charge has not changed after the enemy violated the agreement.

💢To be continued

The case of the online gold dealer has reached the Supreme National Security Council

🔹The online gold sales platform Milli Gold, in a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, has called for an urgent order to lift restrictions on users' access to their gold held in bank vaults.

🔹The platform says restrictions imposed by the Economic Security Police and some related bodies have made it difficult to access part of its reserves and fulfill its obligations to users.

🔹In recent days, a number of Milli Gold users on social media have complained about delays in rial settlements and in receiving their physical gold. Some users have also raised concerns about the actual amount of gold backing the platform's transactions, alleging "selling empty."

🔹These concerns come as, under Central Bank regulations, online platforms must hold reserves equivalent to their obligations for gold sold, and the stored gold must be converted into standard bars with a purity of at least 995 within three months.

🔹Milli Gold, however, claims that existing governance mechanisms and bureaucracy have restricted its access to bank reserves, and that this has in turn disrupted the delivery of users' gold. The company had previously stated that users' gold is held in bank vaults.

🔸Now, given recent concerns about users' access to their gold and the claims raised about the backing of transactions, connecting all platforms to the supervisory system as quickly as possible — with online reporting of their inventory and obligations — has become more important than ever and could ease some of users' concerns.

🔗Read the full report here. @Farsna

Whereas he could have easily glossed over these details and said that he saw the body of the martyred Leader and that his fist was clenched.🔸The matter of honestly declaring "I originally had a different opinion" is another clear example of this aspect of his character, which needs no further explanation.🔸In his condolence message for the passing of Ayatollah Shobeiri Zanjani, various such subtleties can be seen, one of which is this sentence: "This honorable scholar spent his entire noble life—except for the first few years of childhood—on the path of learning and teaching and research"🔸When it is said that a person spent his life on the path of learning and teaching, it does not mean the period of his childhood, but the Supreme Leader of the Revolution does not simply pass over this seemingly obvious matter either, and writes his words with precision and exact details, and specifies that the matter of him having spent his life on this path does not include the first few years of childhood!🔸All this precision and honesty in expression at the highest position of the country is very valuable and, God willing, heralds a much better future.Mohammadreza Nazari🔘 Yes | Eitaa | Soroush+ | Instagram | Telegram@Kayhan_Online

🔹AI…
entry.summary:

Source: @FarsNA

False cheating accusations against students due to software errors

🔹AI detectors used to identify cheating among school and university students have come under scrutiny in new research for significant errors, in some cases mistakenly flagging completely human-written text as AI-generated.

🔹Investigations show these tools do not detect the true origin of the text; instead, they calculate the probability of AI-generated text based on statistical features and writing style.

🔹In one experiment, a completely human-written text was assessed by 5 commercial tools as anywhere from "zero percent" to "100 percent" AI-generated.

🔹These systems have also been reported to make more errors with people whose first language is not English; in a study of 91 real TOEFL essays, an average of 61 percent of human-written texts were mistakenly identified as AI-generated.

🔹Following these problems, universities such as Waterloo in Canada and Cape Town have stopped using Turnitin's AI detection score and have emphasized relying on evidence such as drafts, edit history, learning process, and conversations with the student.

@Farsna - Link

The network's host also asked, citing the killing of protesters and military attacks that contradicted the promises of the head of the Islamic Republic's government: "Who is actually in control of the government in Iran?" In this conversation, Pezeshkian stressed that the Islamic Republic does not want war and claimed that war had been imposed on Iran. He said Tehran is ready to reach an agreement within the framework of international law, but will not accept pressure aimed at forcing the Islamic Republic to surrender. Referring to an agreement and memorandum of understanding that he said had previously been signed with the American side, he spoke of a willingness to continue along that same path, and he held America and Israel responsible for the attacks and for the killing of the former leader of the Islamic Republic, commanders, scientists, and government officials. A significant part of the interview was devoted to the extent of Pezeshkian's authority over the military forces. The host, putting side by side his promise not to use force against protesters, his apology to neighboring countries for the attacks, and the commanders' actions against ships without the knowledge of the "president," asked why his commitments had been violated several times. Pezeshkian first took issue with the casualty figures from the protests. When the host asked again who would guarantee that the IRGC would abide by an agreement he signs, he said groups were supposed to be formed for coordination, clearing up misunderstandings, and creating a channel of communication, but the opportunity to set them up had not been provided. He also accused American forces of firing indiscriminately in the region. The host then asked: "Why should President Trump negotiate with you and not with the IRGC commander, General Vahidi?" In response, Pezeshkian spoke of the deep mistrust between Tehran and Washington and Trump's withdrawal from the JCPOA, but he offered no specific explanation of the limits of his authority vis-à-vis the IRGC commander. 🔰 Iran Cultural Week to Be Held in Four Russian Cities

🔸The Deputy for Scientific and Cultural Cooperation at the Organization of Culture and Islamic Communication announced that the Cultural Week of the Islamic Republic of Iran will be held in four cities — Moscow, Saint Petersburg, Kazan, and Astrakhan — featuring 13 cultural, artistic, scientific, and specialized programs.

🔸Hossein Divsalar, noting the scope of the event, said: This edition of Iran Cultural Week has been designed to present a comprehensive picture of "historical Iran, cultural Iran, and contemporary Iran," and efforts have been made to introduce not only the country's civilizational and cultural heritage but also Iran's present-day capacities in art, knowledge, technology, and cultural products to Russian audiences. He described the geographical reach and diversity of the programs as hallmarks of this edition, adding: In addition to Moscow, programs will be held in Saint Petersburg, Kazan, and Astrakhan. A performance by the Iranian National Music Orchestra at the historic Bolshoi Hall in Moscow, a film and animation week, special programs for children and teenagers, scientific and academic sessions, and a large cultural and artistic exhibition are among the planned events.

🔸The Deputy of the Organization of Culture and Islamic Communication also announced a special focus on creative industries at this event, saying: Areas such as cinema and animation, toys, computer games, and fashion and apparel have been given attention in this edition, and alongside product showcases, specialized sessions and trade negotiations between Iranian and Russian professionals will be held to pave the way for joint cooperation and the entry of Iranian creative products and services into the Russian market. Divsalar, emphasizing that Iran Cultural Week should not be limited to a series of one-off programs, stated: One of the main goals of this event is to build lasting connections among artists, academics, cultural figures, and professional organizations of the two countries.

🔸To that end, the negotiations and connections established during the Cultural Week will be followed up after the programs conclude, in order to lay the groundwork for joint projects and the continuation of cultural cooperation between Iran and Russia.

📢 Details of the meeting between the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran and the Foreign Minister of Germany

◀️ Seyyed Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who has traveled to New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, met and held talks on Wednesday morning on the sidelines of the session with Johann Wadephul, the Foreign Minister of Germany.

◀️ During this meeting, views were exchanged on bilateral relations between Iran and Germany as well as regional and international issues.

◀️ Our country's Foreign Minister, while outlining the positions of the Islamic Republic of Iran regarding international developments, stated that rebuilding trust in the functioning of the United Nations requires all governments to adhere to the principles and objectives of the Charter and international law, and criticized the conduct of European countries, including Germany, for their appeasement of America's law-breaking and bullying.

◀️ The Foreign Minister also, referring to the ongoing occupation and warmongering by the Zionist regime in the West Asia region, described Germany's military and political support, along with that of certain other European countries, as a major factor in the continuation of this regime's crimes against the countries of the region, and stressed the need to stop this kind of complicity in crimes, end impunity, and hold the occupying regime accountable.

◀️ The Foreign Minister further, while explaining Iran's responsible approach in resorting to diplomacy regarding Iran's peaceful nuclear issue, noted: No party can disregard Iran's goodwill in the negotiations and America's and the Zionist regime's military aggression against Iran in the middle of the talks, and portray Iran as the cause of insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz.

◀️ Our country's Foreign Minister emphasized that the Islamic Republic of Iran has conveyed logical conditions and requirements for advancing diplomacy to the American side, and stressed that restoring security to the region requires an end to America's interventionist and aggressive actions against Iran.

◀️ During this meeting, views were also exchanged on bilateral relations and diplomatic and consular consultations between the two countries.

3 questions for Araghchi about the reason for meeting with Witkoff

🔹According to the Foreign Ministry spokesman, the meeting between the Iranian team and Witkoff at the United Nations was held with the aim of conveying Tehran's conditions to the American side. Yet according to explicit statements by Mohsen Rezaei and Baghaei, Iran's conditions had already been conveyed to America through mediators last week. Therefore, questions arise regarding this meeting.

🔸1. As both the Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council and the Foreign Ministry spokesman confirmed, Iran's conditions had been officially conveyed to America last week. Consequently, Washington was aware of Iran's conditions for any negotiations and for ending the war. According to Baghaei's statements, yesterday's meeting between Araghchi and Witkoff was not a new matter, and Iran's conditions were conveyed during this meeting. So the question is: what necessity, achievement, or urgency did holding such a meeting have for Iran?

🔹2. It is no secret that one of the main domestic and foreign pressures on the American government is the rise in oil prices. It is also abundantly clear that holding a meeting with the American side — especially at the United Nations — affects oil prices and reduces that pressure. If America has not yet sent an official response through mediators accepting all of Iran's conditions, what is the necessity of holding such a meeting and bearing its side effects — the reduction of oil prices and, consequently, the reduction of pressure on America?

🔸3. According to the recent statement by Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, America, in coordination with its allies, is planning action against Iran. Any new, high-level military action would deliver a massive shock to the global oil market. Therefore, America needs to bring oil prices down somewhat — even slightly — before taking action, so that afterward, despite the oil shock, the final price does not reach an unexpected figure. Thus, any action that leads to a reduction in oil prices at the current time inadvertently facilitates America's pre-attack needs. The question for the Foreign Minister is: why was the meeting with Witkoff held at such a decisive time?

Kyodo reported that Tehran's new proposal has been approved by "Mojtaba Khamenei," the Leader of the Islamic Republic, and the Supreme National Security Council. The Iranian official did not specify whether the proposal means Tehran is backing away from part of the seven conditions previously put forward for negotiations and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. According to Kyodo's report, the Supreme National Security Council had decided on 25 Mordad that if America does not end the blockade of Iran's ports within 45 days, the Islamic Republic would reserve the option of attacking American forces again. That deadline is now approaching.
